Medical A/R Management

Money You Have Already Earned, Just Not Yet Collected

Accounts receivable is every dollar a practice is owed for services already delivered but not yet paid, whether that balance sits with an insurance payer or a patient. Managing A/R well means knowing exactly how old every claim is, why it has not been paid, and what the next action on it should be, instead of letting balances sit in a queue.

A/R is complex because it is variable by nature. Insurance A/R and patient A/R behave differently, and the complexity and variability of the process is exactly what makes it easy for balances to get stuck. Once a claim passes 90 days, the odds of ever collecting it drop sharply, and past 120 days many practices simply write the balance off.

PMEX gives practices full visibility into A/R performance, including days in A/R, aging distribution and A/R turnover, and runs a structured recovery process on every aging bucket so old claims get worked before they become uncollectable.

Our A/R Recovery Process

A Fixed Cadence for Every Aging Bucket

A/R does not get worked by accident. PMEX runs the same recovery sequence against every outstanding balance, so nothing quietly ages past the point of no return.

0 to 30 Days

Monitor

Claim status tracked automatically. Most balances resolve here without manual work.

31 to 60 Days

First Follow-Up

Payer contacted directly to confirm status and resolve any missing information.

61 to 90 Days

Escalation

Root-cause analysis performed and claims escalated within the payer's process.

91-Plus Days

Recovery Priority

Oldest claims worked first, before timely-filing and appeal windows close.

Insurance vs Patient A/R

Two Balances, Two Different Recovery Playbooks

Insurance A/R and patient A/R fail for different reasons, and treating them the same way is one of the most common causes of stalled collections.

Insurance A/R

  • Payer-specific follow-up on unpaid and underpaid claims
  • Claim status tracking through the payer's own systems
  • Dispute negotiation and appeal management
  • Timely-filing deadline monitoring by payer

Patient A/R

  • Clear statements sent once insurance has adjudicated
  • Reminder notices and structured follow-up on overdue balances
  • Convenient payment options to reduce collection friction
  • Pre-service cost estimates to reduce surprise balances

A/R KPIs

The Numbers That Tell You If A/R Is Under Control

Days in A/R

Average time a dollar sits unpaid, tracked against specialty benchmarks.

A/R Aging Distribution

The share of total A/R sitting in each 30-day bucket.

A/R Turnover

How efficiently outstanding balances convert into collected revenue.

Percent of A/R Over 90 Days

The clearest early warning sign that recovery is falling behind.
